text.p: A 115-year old man received a new pacemaker on Thursday after the batteries ran out on one installed when he was 104, doctors said.

John Bell, born in 1881, was the oldest patient ever to undergo an operation at Johns Hopkins University Hospital, according to Dr. Ronald Berger, the hospital's cardiac electrophysiologist who performed the operation.
Berger said on Friday that installing the new pacemaker was much easier than the original operation 11 years ago, which required running a wire to Bell's heart.
"Replacing a pacemaker is like giving someone food," Berger said. "As long as the rest of the body is working, he deserves to have a heart beat."
